responsibilities: GAIN is seeking to recruit an IT Project Manager-Finance Systems Transformation (Business Central) to manage the implementation of its cloud-based finance management information system, improving financial processes and bringing programme, grant and entity information together across GAIN.

This role will be offered on a 12-month fixed term contract, subject to availability of funding and will be based in Nairobi, Kenya. This advert closes on 6th November 2026. You will understand the finance, budgeting, grants and reporting needs of non-profit organisations and have delivered projects across multiple countries or entities.

You will be comfortable connecting finance and technical teams, translating requirements clearly and securing action from colleagues and suppliers without relying on line-management authority. Organised and analytical, you will balance attention to detail with overall delivery priorities, manage competing demands against a fixed deadline and exercise sound judgement when resolving or escalating issues. Strong written and spoken English, clear reporting and the ability to collaborate across time zones are essential, alongside experience helping users adopt new systems through training, change support and operational handover.

jobs.title: IT Support Associate NGO Job Food For Education
jobs.description: IT Jobs, Food For Education Jobs. Responsible for providing technical support to staff, troubleshooting hardware and software issues, maintaining IT equipment, managing user accounts, and ensuring reliable network and system operations. Requires a diploma or degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related field. This is a full-time, on-site position based in Nairobi
responsibilities: F4E runs a large, distributed operation of more than 5,500 staff. Kitchens cook meals for hundreds of thousands of children every school day. Field teams track deliveries, manage stock, and report on every site. Our Service Centre staff, more than 400 of them, support field teams and keep us executing on our long-term strategy. All of this depends on technology that works: devices that turn on, networks that connect, and hardware that doesn’t fail mid-service.

As IT Support Associate, you are the hands-on first line of that promise. You are the first person colleagues come to when technology gets in their way, and you are the one who keeps devices, networks and sites working across HQ, warehouses, kitchens and field locations. You keep the support queue moving, you keep the asset register honest, and when the Manager, IT Support is running a rollout, you are the person delivering it on the ground.

This is a delivery role rather than a strategy role, and that is deliberate. The Manager sets the roadmap, the standards and the escalation path. You execute against them, you work independently once the standard is clear, and you bring back what the field is telling you. It is a role with real scope and a clear path: build operational discipline here and your ownership grows with it.
requirements: Experience administering Google Workspace and/or Microsoft 365.
Familiarity with an IT ticketing system such as Jira or equivalent.
Basic understanding of cybersecurity principles and safe IT practices.
Certification such as CompTIA A+, Microsoft Certified Fundamentals or equivalent.
Experience using AI tools for automation, scripting or building quick prototypes, for example Copilot, ChatGPT or Claude.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer NGO Job Living Goods
jobs.description: IT Jobs, Living Goods Jobs. The Senior Software Engineer leads software development and engineering teams, requires a CS/IT degree and 7+ years software development experience (with 2+ years in a senior/lead role). Full-time role in Nairobi.
responsibilities: Set the technical direction for your product area: decide the architecture, write the design down before the first ticket is cut, and record the decisions and the reasoning behind them.
Lead a team of two to four engineers – break work down, sequence it against real dependencies, and clear what is blocking other people before your own tasks.
Use code review as the primary teaching instrument: raise the standard of what gets merged and leave the author better prepared for the next change.
Mentor and grow mid-level Software engineers through pairing, structured feedback and handing over work that stretches them.
Represent engineering with product managers, programme teams and Ministry of Health stakeholders – translating constraints into plans, and deadlines into honest scope conversations.
Own the health of what your team ships: dependable CI, uneventful releases, test coverage where it earns its keep, and technical debt named openly rather than absorbed quietly.
requirements: Bachelor’s degree in computer science, IT, Software Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
7+ years of professional software development experience, including at least 2 years leading a team or serving as the senior engineer other developers depended on.
Demonstrated depth in either the JVM (Kotlin or Java) or TypeScript and Node.js, with the willingness to work across both – our platform is not single-language and neither is this role.
Proven track record of shipping and then maintaining production software: a mobile application with real users in the field, or backend services carrying meaningful load.
Hands-on experience designing, developing and implementing fit-for-purpose digital solutions at scale, preferably in the digital health space.

jobs.title: CIS Engineer Job U.S. Embassy
jobs.description: IT Jobs, U.S. Embassy Jobs. Responsible for maintaining and supporting computer information systems, managing system security, and ensuring reliable IT operations in line with organisational requirements. Requires a degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field, with 3 years of relevant experience. This is a full-time, on-site position based in Nairobi.
responsibilities: The Communication Infrastructure Support (CIS) Engineer is responsible for the engineering and designing of various communication systems for Mission Nairobi. The incumbent actively installs, maintains, repairs, and cables Embassy telephone equipment, including programming the CS1000 telephone and CallPilot systems, as well as the Cisco Unified Communications Manager (CUCM) and Unity messaging Connection. Additionally, the incumbent is responsible for designing, installing, maintaining, and repairing Post’s seven radio networks.
They maintain equipment for the radio network, such as digital repeaters, handheld radios, base stations, antennas, and mobile radios.

The incumbent supports the unclassified networking infrastructure at several locations, including the main Chancery, Acacia, OAK, Chief of Mission Residences (CMR), and Deputy Chief of Mission Residences (DCMR), including OpenNet, Non-Enterprise Network (NEN) switches, routers, and a firewall. The incumbent manages microwave point-to-point networks across 7 Local Area Network (LAN) tail sites throughout the city. The CIS engineer works closely with the Mission’s Internet Service Providers (ISP) across 20 Wide Area Networks (WAN) circuits, actively monitoring service degradation and troubleshooting connection issues while maintaining the maximum possible uptime.

They collaborate with ENM, ITSC, and other Washington program offices to configure VPN devices, troubleshoot network latency, monitor line availability, and client switch configurations. The incumbent also assists the Audio-Visual technicians with infrastructure setups and running high-profile meetings utilizing sound mixers, wireless microphones, and camera equipment.
requirements: All selected candidates will be subject to a background investigation and may be subject to a pre-employment medical exam.
Selected candidate must be able to begin working within a reasonable period of time upon receipt of agency authorization and/or clearances/certifications or their candidacy may end.
